fns.desc: wpa_priv_cmd_authenticate's bounds check `sizeof(*auth) + auth->ie_len + auth->auth_data_len > len` can integer-overflow: ie_len/auth_data_len are size_t fields read directly from the (world-writable, 0777-permissioned per chmod at line 852) privsep datagram, fully controlled by whatever local peer sends to the socket. A crafted sum near SIZE_MAX wraps below len, passing the check, after which params.ie_len/params.auth_data_len are set to the huge attacker-controlled values while params.ie/params.auth_data point into the small 2000-byte stack buffer, causing a large out-of-bounds read when passed to iface->driver->authenticate(). Local-privesc-adjacent since the socket is world-writable.

wpa_priv_cmd_associate's bounds check `sizeof(*assoc) + assoc->wpa_ie_len > len` has the same integer-overflow shape as wpa_priv_cmd_authenticate (line 260): wpa_ie_len is an attacker/peer-controlled size_t that can wrap the sum below len, then params.wpa_ie_len is set to the oversized value while params.wpa_ie points into the small stack buffer.
